title: fix: preserve KPI secrets during application deployments
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Removes unconditional secret synchronization from KPI deployments so application rollouts preserve the existing Worker credentials.
- Stops requesting SOPS access for the KPI deploy job; separately approved credential changes remain separate operations.
- Validated the deployment manifest and application-discovery tests.

gist.headline: Credentials stay planted
gist.blurb: KPI application rollouts now leave their existing Worker credentials tucked safely in the soil. Secret changes remain their own deliberate gardening task.
gist.summary: KPI deployments no longer unconditionally synchronize secrets or request SOPS access, preserving existing Worker credentials during application rollouts.
gist.impact: KPI application updates can roll out without overwriting their established Worker credentials, while approved secret changes continue through separate operations.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy KPI deployment garden where Polli carefully replants a small application sprout while a locked credential seed jar remains safely untouched on a nearby shelf. A retro terminal can show a simple deploy status, with flowers and code-vines reinforcing that deployments and secret management are separate, orderly tasks.
